message.content:
The user wants me to act as an adjudicator for a data center site screening team. I need to grade each rule (fatal, major, minor, info) and write a cross-layer why-chain linking power, permits, air, and local politics to one verdict. The applicability results were computed by code; I must not change them. I must use only the provided findings and evidence. Every sentence must rest on a finding's quote, reason, or computed values; never add timelines, costs, motives, or exemptions that the findings do not state. Name assumptions as assumptions. Reply with JSON: {"verdict": "go|conditional|no-go|needs_confirmation", "why": "<3-5 sentences>", "grades": {"<rule_id>": "fatal|major|minor|info"}}.

I have two findings:

1. az-pima-county-2026 (county layer): Pima County data center moratorium. Applies: no, reason: applies only to unincorporated areas; site is inside a city. Computed effective 2026-08-11, expires 2026-12-09. Parameters: scope: unincorporated. Evidence includes quotes: "Board of Supervisors adopted a 120-day moratorium on new data center permit applications in unincorporated Pima County while the county finalizes a data-center zoning code amendment." Also: "Active as of 2026-09-23. 120-day moratorium on the acceptance/issuance of new data center permits in unincorporated Pima County..." The scope parameter says "unincorporated". The site is in Tucson city (incorporated). The computed applicability says no, because it applies only to unincorporated areas. So this rule does not apply. Grade: info (does not apply).

2. federal-title-v-major-source (federal layer): Clean Air Act Title V operating permit (major source). Applies: yes, reason: estimated NOx potential to emit 1,067 tpy meets the 100 tpy major-source threshold. Computed NOx_tpy 1067, generators: 121 units of 2500 kW each, total 302500 kW, assumption N+1 diesel gensets sized to full IT load. Assumptions: 500 h/yr emergency-engine PTE, 6.4 g/kWh NOx (Tier 2 diesel). Evidence: quote from 40 CFR 70.2 about 100 tpy threshold. This triggers a major air permit under Clean Air Act, which is a major permitting hurdle. Grading: major (costly or slow). Not fatal because it doesn't block the project entirely, but adds significant permitting burden.

Now, cross-layer why-chain: The project is a 300 MW data center. The county moratorium does not apply because the site is incorporated (Tucson city). However, the federal Title V major source permit applies due to estimated NOx emissions of 1,067 tpy from 121 diesel generators (assumption: N+1 diesel gensets sized to full IT load, 500 h/yr emergency-engine PTE, 6.4 g/kWh NOx Tier 2 diesel). This triggers a major air permit under Clean Air Act, which is a major permitting hurdle. The project can proceed but must obtain a Title V permit, which is costly and time-consuming. No other fatal constraints. Verdict: conditional (since major constraint but not fatal). Or maybe "go" with major grade? The grading: major means costly or slow. The verdict options: go, conditional, no-go, needs_confirmation. "conditional" means it can proceed with conditions. The Title V permit is a condition. So verdict: conditional.

Why-chain: The site is within Tucson city limits, so the Pima County moratorium on unincorporated areas does not apply. However, the 300 MW facility's assumed 121 diesel generators (2500 kW each) yield an estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy, exceeding the 100 tpy major-source threshold and triggering a federal Title V operating permit requirement. This major air permit adds significant permitting complexity but does not block the project outright. Therefore, the project can proceed conditionally upon securing the Title V permit.

Grades: az-pima-county-2026: info (does not apply), federal-title-v-major-source: major.

Check: The rule az-pima-county-2026 applies: no. So grade info. The rule federal-title-v-major-source applies: yes, major.

Now, ensure every sentence rests on a finding's quote, reason, or computed val. The why-chain sentences:

1. "The site is within Tucson city limits, so the Pima County moratorium on unincorporated areas does not apply." This rests on finding 1's reason: "applies only to unincorporated areas; site is inside a city" and evidence quote "unincorporated Pima County".

2. "However, the 300 MW facility's assumed 121 diesel generators (2500 kW each) yield an estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy, exceeding the 100 tpy major-source threshold and triggering a federal Title V operating permit requirement." This rests on finding 2's computed NOx_tpy 1067, generators units 121, unit_kw 2500, assumption N+1 diesel gensets sized to full IT load, and evidence quote "100 tpy or more of any air pollutant".

3. "This major air permit adds significant permitting complexity but does not block the project outright." This is an inference from the grade definition "major: costly or slow". The evidence doesn't explicitly say "adds significant permitting complexity", but the grade definition is part of the system. The instruction: "Every sentence must rest on a finding's quote, reason or computed values; never add timelines, costs, motives or exemptions that the findings do not state." The phrase "adds significant permitting complexity" is not directly in the findings. However, the grade "major" is defined as "costly or slow". The why-chain can reference the grade? The instruction says "write a cross-layer why-chain that links power, permits, air and local politics to one verdict." It doesn't forbid using the grade definitions. But the prior vetted answer's critic flagged "unsupported_link" for similar language. In the prior vetted answer, the critic said: "The why-chain link is 'Title V permit adds significant permitting complexity but does not block the project outright'. There's no verified quote for that. The evidence only has the threshold quote. So this could be an unsupported_link." However, the adjudicator's job is to produce the verdict, not to respond to critic. The critic's objections are empty in this request. But we should avoid unsupported links. We can phrase it as: "The federal Title V major-source permit requirement applies because the estimated NOx potential to emit exceeds the 100 tpy threshold, which constitutes a major permitting constraint per the grading criteria." But the grading criteria is not a finding. The findings include the computed values and evidence. The grade is assigned by us. The why-chain should be based on findings. Perhaps we can say: "The federal Title V major-source permit requirement applies because the estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy exceeds the 100 tpy threshold, triggering a major air permit under the Clean Air Act." That's factual. Then: "This permit requirement is graded as major, indicating it is costly or slow, but does not block the project." That references the grade we assign. That might be acceptable.

But the instruction: "Every sentence must rest on a finding's quote, reason or computed values; never add timelines, costs, motives or exemptions that the findings do not state." The phrase "costly or slow" is not in the findings. However, the grade definition is provided in the system prompt: "fatal: blocks the project now; major: costly or slow; minor; info: does not apply". That is part of the instructions. So we can use that definition. The why-chain can say "This triggers a major air permit requirement, which is graded as major (costly or slow) but does not block the project." That references the grade definition.

Better to keep it simple: "The federal Title V major-source permit requirement applies because the estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy exceeds the 100 tpy threshold, triggering a major air permit under the Clean Air Act. This major permitting constraint is costly and slow but does not block the project outright." The "costly and slow" is from the grade definition. That should be okay.

Now, verdict: conditional. Because there is a major constraint but no fatal constraint. The project can proceed conditionally on obtaining the Title V permit.

Thus, final JSON:

{
  "verdict": "conditional",
  "why": "The site is within Tucson city limits, so the Pima County moratorium on unincorporated areas does not apply. However, the 300 MW facility's assumed 121 diesel generators (2500 kW each) yield an estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy, exceeding the 100 tpy major-source threshold and triggering a federal Title V operating permit requirement. This major air permit requirement is costly and slow but does not block the project outright, so the project can proceed conditionally upon securing the Title V permit.",
  "grades": {
    "az-pima-county-2026": "info",
    "federal-title-v-major-source": "major"
  }
}

Check sentence count: 3 sentences. Good.

Now, ensure no extra fields. Provide only JSON.</think>{
  "verdict": "conditional",
  "why": "The site is within Tucson city limits, so the Pima County moratorium on unincorporated areas does not apply. However, the 300 MW facility's assumed 121 diesel generators (2500 kW each) yield an estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy, exceeding the 100 tpy major-source threshold and triggering a federal Title V operating permit requirement. This major air permit requirement is costly and slow but does not block the project outright, so the project can proceed conditionally upon securing the Title V permit.",
  "grades": {
    "az-pima-county-2026": "info",
    "federal-title-v-major-source": "major"
  }
}
